parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Well, today we're focusing on New Zealand in the 1860s and in particular, how the discovery of gold transformed the country. At that time, gold had created great wealth in North America and Australia, and naturally, New Zealand was hoping for the same success. People knew there was gold in New Zealand. Some had been found in 1852, leading to a brief gold rush in which people had come from all parts of the world to see if they could dig up any for themselves. But now New Zealand needed experienced gold prospectors, people who knew where to look for the stuff to find in other areas. So what the local government started doing in the late 1850s was promising a reward if these prospectors discovered gold anywhere in their province.

The man who eventually answered the call was an Australian miner called Gabrielle Reed, who came to Otago in May 1861. The story goes that he was walking outside his tent at night when he saw gold shining like stars in a nearby river. It didn't take long for word of his fine to spread, and soon thousands were coming to Otago to take part in the gold rush. Who were these people? Well, the men that came were predominantly laborers and tradesmen and often very young, although some were married and left their families back in the countries they came from. But women did come, too, to the towns that suddenly sprang up by the gold fields. They made a living by starting up hotels, simple ones, of course, where new arrivals would often stay. And then there were businessmen who knew there was money to be made by setting up services like hardware stores that sold mining and camping equipment. And of course, banks where gold could be deposited. In fact, the businessmen often did better than the minors.

So as I mentioned before, where there was a gold field, a town began to grow, too. At first, the buildings were constructed in a temporary fashion, just made out of material such as canvas and timber. But later, once supply started arriving, it was concrete. So the structures became more permanent. But the fact was the gold fields were often in very isolated areas. So life was very difficult for these people. The miners were often working at the bottom of deep gorges, so they had to cope with freezing temperatures and also sudden flooding when winter ice melted in the mountains. If this wasn't bad enough, the miners also had to deal with another problem, because they had to carry everything with them, they had a very poor diet. They mostly drank tea. And the main thing they had to eat was flour, which they cooked in different ways. That's all that was available anyway. Some miners were lucky, others not.

But the goal that was found certainly brought many benefits to the Otago region and also a couple of problems. First of all, the town of Deneden was suddenly transformed into the biggest city in New Zealand. Some of the original residents complained about how the value of land was increasing and about the inadequate sanitation. You can imagine how crowded it might have felt with the sudden influx of thousands of immigrants. But overall, the gold brought many positive changes to the city. There was immense investment and growth in the shipping industry, just what the region needed. Another unexpected benefit of this wealth was that it provided the funds for the first university in the country. As well as this, as the industry developed. There was a great demand for workers of all sorts, but most of all, there was a demand for experienced and skilled engineers. They often started their own companies, and many of these companies are still operating today. What we will discover next week is that these companies are still.

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到政府承诺如果能发现黄金就会给予 prospectors 一笔 reward。
So what the local government started doing in the late 1850s was promising a reward if these prospectors discovered gold anywhere in their province.
不要因为听到 promise 就去寻找类似词汇，注意听后文“reward”这个核心词。

The story goes that he was walking outside his tent at night when he saw gold shining like stars in a nearby river. It didn't take long for word of his fine to spread, and soon thousands were coming to Otago to take part in the gold rush.
注意不要漏听“in a nearby river”这个具体的发现地点。
录音中提到 Gabriel Read 是在附近的河流里看到了像星星一样闪烁的黄金。
But women did come, too, to the towns that suddenly sprang up by the gold fields. They made a living by starting up hotels, simple ones, of course, where new arrivals would often stay.
注意听到“starting up hotels”时不要犹豫，这就是答案。
录音中说女性来到矿区后通过开设简易的旅馆（hotels）来维持生计。

And then there were businessmen who knew there was money to be made by setting up services like hardware stores that sold mining and camping equipment. And of course, banks where gold could be deposited.
不要只盯着前面的 hardware stores，注意听并列的另一个服务。
录音中列举了商人提供的服务，其中明确提到了人们可以存金子的银行（banks）。

At first, the buildings were constructed in a temporary fashion, just made out of material such as canvas and timber. But later, once supply started arriving, it was concrete. So the structures became more permanent.
注意区分建筑材料的演变过程，不要错填成起初的材料。
录音中对比了建筑材料的变化，起初是帆布和木材，后来随着供应充足，变成了混凝土（concrete）。
录音提到矿工在深谷工作时，除了要应对严寒，还要面对冰雪融化引发的突然洪水（flooding）。
The miners were often working at the bottom of deep gorges, so they had to cope with freezing temperatures and also sudden flooding when winter ice melted in the mountains.
注意“unexpected”对应录音中的“sudden”，确认填入洪水这个灾害。

If this wasn't bad enough, the miners also had to deal with another problem, because they had to carry everything with them, they had a very poor diet. They mostly drank tea. And the main thing they had to eat was flour, which they cooked in different ways.
注意题目中的“flower”是发音干扰项，录音说的是“flour”，千万别拼错了。
录音中说矿工饮食很差，除了喝茶，主要的食物就是面粉（flour）。
Some of the original residents complained about how the value of land was increasing and about the inadequate sanitation.
注意听 complaints 后面的具体内容，不要遗漏“value of land”中的核心词。
录音中明确提到当地居民抱怨土地（land）价值上涨的问题。
Another unexpected benefit of this wealth was that it provided the funds for the first university in the country.
注意“funds for the first university”这个结构，不要把资金来源（funds）误当成建设的目标。
录音中提到黄金带来的意想不到的好处之一是资助了该国的第一所大学（university）。
As well as this, as the industry developed. There was a great demand for workers of all sorts, but most of all, there was a demand for experienced and skilled engineers.
注意听“in particular”之后的强调内容，这就是题目对应的核心答案。
录音中提到随着行业发展，对于各类工人需求很大，尤其是经验丰富的工程师
